rationale: These recordings have no artifact rejection, so blinks, movement and electrode pops inflate the mean-averaged Welch PSD. That distorts the relative power, mostly in the delta, theta and gamma bands that carry the theta/beta signal. I'm changing Welch to take the median over segments instead of the mean, which suppresses short high-amplitude artifacts without any explicit epoch rejection and holds up across amplifiers and recording lengths. I also replace NaN or inf features with 0 before scaling, to guard against flat channels.

I'm adding a per-channel aperiodic (1/f) exponent for each condition alongside the existing log relative band powers. It is a least-squares slope of log-power against log-frequency over 2–40 Hz, leaving out the alpha band (7–14 Hz). ADHD is linked to a flatter exponent, which is thought to reflect a shift in the balance of cortical excitation and inhibition. A slope doesn't change when the signal is rescaled, so it should hold up across amplifiers. It also helps separate genuine oscillatory theta/beta differences from broadband tilt, which relative band power mixes together.

I'm adding one new feature: the aperiodic (1/f) exponent for each channel and condition. It comes from a log-log linear fit of the Welch PSD over 2–40 Hz, leaving out the alpha region (7–14 Hz). The slope is thought to reflect the excitation/inhibition balance and has been reported to differ in ADHD. Relative band powers mix this background slope with oscillatory peaks and can't separate the two. The slope also stays the same if the signal's amplitude is rescaled, which helps when the model is applied to recordings from other clinics.

It should give cleaner relative band power estimates, including theta/beta, and stay robust to recording length and amplifier differences.

I'm switching the Welch PSD from mean to median averaging across segments. The recordings have no artifact rejection, so short bursts like eye blinks in EO (mostly delta/theta) and muscle activity (mostly beta/gamma) can dominate the averaged band powers and hide the small theta/beta differences linked to ADHD. A median over the 2-s segments estimates the background spectrum and largely ignores those transient segments. This is untested here, so I don't have a score for it yet. I also added a small epsilon so a flat channel can't produce log(0).
